style_when: the story is regulatory or contractual — a filing, a mandate, a rate notice, a certificate, a purchase order that changed the economics
prompt: Overhead flat-lay photograph of a thick printed remodeling contract resting asymmetrically on a weathered wooden kitchen table. Asymmetric top-down 90-degree view, even diffused daylight illuminating the matte paper stock. The document is slightly out of alignment to look handled, with the bottom page revealing a bold cancellation notice block next to a blank signature line. Muted paper tones, crisp focal plane, generous editorial negative space on the textured wooden surface, sophisticated color palette.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random letters, numbers, UI, watermarks, printed lettering, people, hands, faces
rationale: The story revolves entirely around a legal and contractual mechanism—the physical contract, its signature line, and the location where it is signed. Document flatlay perfectly captures this regulatory turning point.
subject: remodeling contract on a kitchen table
core_thesis: The federal three-day cancellation window for remodeling deposits depends strictly on whether the contract was signed at home or in a showroom.
core_conflict: Federal consumer protection versus binding showroom contract.
